t:
It's a pity. I saw great potential in you, and you give up your future to protect some natives from another world. Everyone in Sarnaut will know about your decision!

And even if you change your mind, coming back will not be easy!

This is good news, but I want to make sure you don't falter at the crucial moment.

Is that right?

Great, I knew you could be counted on. Some natives from another world are less important than saving all of Sarnaut! I will try to let everyone in Sarnaut know about your feat.

Once everything is decided, remember that even if you change your mind, the Children are unlikely to welcome you back with open arms!
The Expedition is counting on you. We have a lot of problems in this world. The most important is the Ambrosia.

That's how we wanted it to go when we sent you with Waterlily. But as you can see, you didn't get anywhere. Perhaps you managed to find allies among the Children who can act as an intermediary? What about this Waterlily?

I already got that. Although when I sent you to negotiate with them, I thought we could find some common ground. As for Waterlily, she didn't seem to be as antagonistic. Perhaps it will be possible to establish communications through her?

I don't see any room for compromise yet. We desperately need the Ambrosia, and the Children are zealously guarding their trees...

And if I understand the ideas of this All-Mother correctly, she does not want the worlds created by her to follow the path of technological development.
Then you should do everything to win her over to our side. But as far as I remember, Skulnar the Fierce and Eurial went with you. For some reason I don't see them with you - where are they now?

This proves that the Children are fanatical. They believe in their goddess. Fortunately, we have experience in fighting gods and those who believe in them. However, I have a question. Skulnar the Fierce and Eurial were with you. Where are they now?

Is that so?

I always suspected that Zayan’s apprentices couldn't be trusted. While we needed Skulnar as a navigator on the Star Trail, the viper had no place here.

Fortunately, we can do without them now. The path is clear, the Gates can create a passage from Sarnaut to Eden without any help. And if we need to get into another world, we will find someone else for the job.

The only thing I don't understand is... Which side are you on?

I knew it!

Zayan’s apprentices can't trusted, and neither can Klavdia. All these Orders of Creation and Balance are nothing but trouble. When Felix and I return to Sarnaut, we will deal with them all.

And Felix has already warned me that Skulnar the Fierce is very dangerous. Over time, he and his orcs will become a real threat to the Empire which is currently our ally. And as they say, the enemy of my enemy... is my enemy!

And Eurial is the daughter of Elleken, the Great Mage who has been wanted by the Conclave for crimes for over a millennium. She is his supporter and accomplice.

Fortunately, we can do without them now. The path is clear, the Gates can create a passage from Sarnaut to Eden without any help. And if we need to get into another world, we will find someone else for the job.

The only thing I don't understand is... Which side are you on?

Yes, you are the only one who hasn't decided yet. You need to make a choice.

If these Children and their goddess are so dear to you, you can go to them. I'm only letting you do this because I remember your past exploits. But the next time we meet, we'll be enemies. And if you are willing to defend our world, then I will be glad to see you in our ranks.

Whose side are you on? Decide! It's now or never!

You learned my lessons, so I didn't doubt your decision. I see this Expedition does not represent everyone who lives in your world. You, Eurial, and Skulnar can stay in my domain.

However, I see the threat coming from Catherina and Felix. They can't win, but they can do enough damage.

You will have to banish them, just as you banished Hirkalla. Help my Children, and they will give you everything my world has to offer.
Yes, Child of Sarn. Once we are victorious, I will go with you to your world. If my lost daughter is crying out for help, how can I refuse?

I do not know much about military affairs, but my Children have been steadily improving in recent months, preparing to repel the onslaught of the enemy. They defeated the Old Tribe with your help, now this knowledge will be used to fight the Expedition. Rhubarb will tell you the rest.
Here is the thing. Catherina sent a message telling everyone to come back. I think you understand what that means.

Sort of. The scouts report that the Mechanoids are heading for the Valley.

Which means there will be another fight here soon, nuts and bolts flying every which way.

However, if Felix thinks everything will be simple, he'll be disappointed. The Children are also decent warriors, and they are getting stronger every day.

Yep. They didn't want to wait until we're finished here. Though I doubt they actually expected us to do anything. We were probably sent here like lambs to be slaughtered, with the expectation that the All-Mother would condemn us and this would be his... what was it... casus belli, yes.

But this Xadaganian is fooling himself if he thinks this fight will be a cakewalk. The Children are already good warriors, they trained while we were just sitting here.

Yeah, sort of. The peacekeeping mission turned into simple recon, heh. The Committee loved doing that back in the day. Well, we've seen a lot...

But I'll tell you what - this battle won't be easy. There are considerable forces on the side of the Children, and they are, in fact, not bad warriors. If Felix sticks his head in here, there will be losses.

Me? Well, it wasn't Catherina who sent us to this world, but Klavdia, so I will try to do what she asked us to do. Try to persuade the mother to help against Nihaz, that is.

And what the Expedition is doing there doesn't really matter to me. Life, you know, taught me to stay away from all these Xadaganian mechanical things. I think you understand me.

The most important question is what you're planning to do, heh.

In a situation like this, I'm on my side first and foremost, heh. I'd rather keep my head.

But look, Klavdia sent us here, right? She knew Catherina and Felix would start something, so she told us to find the All-Mother and ask for help. The war with the Children will not help our mission in any way - rather the opposite, heh.

 In short, our goal is to save Sarnaut, not the Expedition.  You do as you wish, and I will stay here.

You think so? But I'm not sure. Look, Klavdia sent us here, right? What did she tell us?

Help Catherina and Co.? Or make arrangements with the All-Mother?

The latter. And if we start fighting with the Children now, what will happen? Will we reach agreement? Or we'll get beans? And what about Nihaz, then? He'll just come and destroy everything?

In short, you do as you wish, but I prefer to stay away from this Felix. I'll sit here, heh.
Wow, looks like we're in a bind.
Apparently our friends at the camp did not wait for the end of your training. Now we have to decide what we're going to do.

That's right. The Children or the Expedition.

On the one hand, representatives of our home world who came here for the Ambrosia. A power that has the potential to make us gods.

And then there are the Children, the inhabitants of this world who shouldn't have to suffer because we need this resource. And a powerful goddess who seems to be able to help us.

The choice is not easy.

What do I do? I know better than anyone in Sarnaut what it's like to follow the path that Nihaz mapped out for you. And you know, I don't think that's right at all.

It's great to be powerful - but at what cost? Elleken committed unthinkable atrocities for his own purposes. Tep doomed his people. Ath-Zak was a hero who rejected the temptations of Nihaz. So what do I want to be? A hero or a villain?

Yes, I noticed that you are learning the lessons of the All-Mother. And Skulnar is also leaning towards the Children. But what should I do? You see, my father would of course have chosen to side with the Expedition, but right now I'm not so sure that I want to be on the same side.

I know better than anyone in Sarnaut what it's like to follow the path that Nihaz mapped out for you. And you know, I don't think that's right at all.

It's great to be powerful - but at what cost? Elleken committed unthinkable atrocities for his own purposes. Tep doomed his people. Ath-Zak was a hero who rejected the temptations of Nihaz. So what do I want to be? A hero or a villain?

Yes, I saw you running errands for them. But it looks like Skulnar is leaning towards the Children. But what should I do? You see, my father would of course have chosen to side with the Expedition, but right now I'm not so sure that I want to be on the same side.

I know better than anyone in Sarnaut what it's like to follow the path that Nihaz mapped out for you. And you know, I don't think that's right at all.

It's great to be powerful - but at what cost? Elleken committed unthinkable atrocities for his own purposes. Tep doomed his people. Ath-Zak was a hero who rejected the temptations of Nihaz. So what do I want to be? A hero or a villain?

Obviously, we must help the Children defend their world. I think it would be right.

But if you want to help the Expedition, I won't judge you for that choice. Though I'll be sorry if our ways part.

I don't think the All-Mother is right about everything, but I'm not sure Catherina and Felix should be followed either.

I'm glad you agree with me. So we'll be on the same side. Sarnaut's interests are not focused on ravaging other worlds. Verbena told me that Nihaz had plundered many worlds, stealing their power. We must choose another way.

We will help the Children defend their home and drive back the invaders who do not represent all of Sarnaut.

It's a pity you don't agree with me. So we'll be fighting on different sides. But Sarnaut's interests are not focused on ravaging other worlds. Verbena told me that Nihaz had plundered many worlds, stealing their power. We must choose another way.

Yes, the members of the Expedition are our compatriots. Not all of them, though. I think it's more important to protect this world which could be our ally!

Oh, Catherina. She has always been ambitious. I thought Sarn's story would be a lesson for her, but alas.

To challenge a goddess whose powers we don't even know? Start a war in a foreign world without thinking about the consequences?

Catherina, Felix, and this Ivan must be stopped.

I don't know how, and I don't want to be the one whose words lead to sacrifice. However, I think these Children have every right to defend themselves. After all, this is their world, they are the masters there, and we are the guests.

Try to find Expedition members who are on your side.

It saddens me to hear that innocent people suffer from the actions of those who live in the same world as I do.

The inhabitants of Eden do not deserve to be threatened with weapons and have their resources stolen. After all, they didn’t do us any harm, they didn’t even know we existed until recently.

I think you should help these... Children.

Although it is difficult to stand against your own people, sometimes it's necessary. We were wrong when Citovras and I went after Kyros and almost caused the destruction of the Gift that allows you to rise from the dead.

We were bound by an oath, but now I think perhaps we should have spoken to Kyros and tried to dissuade him.

Neither Klavdia nor Catherina consulted me when they started building these Gates-3. Now you are reaping the fruits of your own recklessness. The Observatory's gaze is directed into the future, and I can say that the likelihood of the Darkness coming to our world has not decreased, but increased.

Nihaz and his followers are cunning - they will find a way to turn everything you do to their advantage.

Luckily for you, I have taken steps of my own to repel a future onslaught on Sarnaut.

I don't see any steps you could take to remedy the situation right now. Catherina and Klavdia put us at a disadvantage in the negotiations - we set these Children against ourselves while being forced to ask the All-Mother for something.

I think we need to wait for the resolution of this conflict. And what role you will play in it depends only on you.

I'll give you one piece of advice - beware of Hirkalla. This "daughter" of Nihaz is extremely dangerous. Perhaps in some ways even more dangerous than her "father".
Stormbringer... I haven't seen you in a while.

You bring some very interesting news...

Well, I assumed there were many interesting things outside of our world...

And now, our task - of the Elves and the House de Delice, is to become ambassadors to these many worlds... I think we'll find a reasonable approach.

As for Catherina and these Children... I'm wary of giving you advice.

We need to find a solution that would satisfy both parties.

But remember this - you and I are residents of Sarnaut and must act in our own interests first and foremost.

Finding a compromise on our terms is your task.

Oh, I knew Catherina would do something like this. Cutting down the Great Trees... How absurd.

No, this cannot be allowed to happen... We need to stop her... How? I'm afraid I'm not ready to advise you. I believe there will be those who can help you.

We need to find those who will agree to side with the All-Mother and protect the Great Trees.

Despite the fact that the Expedition members were handpicked by Felix and Catherina, there have to be those who are not comfortable with what's happening. Pay attention to the Gibberlings - they know what the Great Tree means to us. Perhaps the Pridens will also remember Howlem and what saved it?

Surely there are Kanians who do not trust Catherina.. And while I do not believe it myself, maybe the orc shamans will be on our side?

Extreme fertility!

Look at this - just plant a seed here, turn your back for a couple of seconds - and the sprout is already reaching for the sky. I can imagine how greedily it absorbs nutrients from the soil...

We need Ammer soil in the New Land!

I see. Another world, a world where the Sparks go... Interesting.

After learning about Nihaz and Sarn, I assumed that sooner or later we would meet other gods who are just as cruel and indifferent to the interests of mortals.

But it turns out that everything that exists is the result of some goddess's actions... The goddess who wants to continue the eternal cycle of Life and Death.

I need to think about this.

What advice can I give you?

Our entire history, the history of the Zem people, is a search for victory over death.

Therefore, from the point of view of this... All-Mother, we are quite the heretics.

And while Catherina's and Felix's attempts to lay claim to resources in a foreign world might seem wrong, I'm afraid we have no other choice. We need technology based on the Ambrosia - with it, we'll be able to impose our will on the gods.

[Ollum looks worried]

Waves of emotions emanate from the demon. Eventually you figure out what he is trying to convey.

The demons would like to find a new world, but neither Catherina nor the All-Mother are good options for them.

The ambitious sorceress wouldn't want to let the demons out of Sarnaut while the ancient goddess's thinking rejects the idea of demons altogether.]

Interesting! It’s a bit of a pity that I didn’t get to take part in this Expedition… But they don't trust me since I'm an orc, heh.

Felix was put in charge, and only the most reliable orcs were selected.

Therefore, I wish you success. But as a veteran, I will watch from the sidelines.

What advice do you want from me?

We are the residents of Sarnaut, which means we must act in the interests of our world, and not some other.

Moreover, we don't need those who want to impose their will. We will impose our own order! The time of Trees and shamans has long passed...

What?! This girl thinks too much of herself, hah.

If I see her, I'll thrash her with a belt. Right there in the square. I'll show her a damn rebellion...

Oh, my daughter. Yes, the trouble is, while the father was shedding blood on the frontline, the troublemaker grew up as bold as brass.

In short, tell her I'm going to thrash her with a belt when I see her. Right there in the square. I'll show her a damn rebellion...

Haha, foolish mortals. This elf deceived you... But that's your problem, so deal with it yourself.

When the dragons wanted to leave this world, we would never have gone to this world of Life.

We heard rumors about the activities of this goddess, and Sheratan once saw how she briefly approached Sarnaut, crushing the Child of Order.

She is not needed here.

Get out of the World of Life as quickly as possible. You won't find anything there that will benefit you.

All these promises are just lies.

If you are looking for the Great Trees, then it's better to look for them in Sarnaut.

It's you again, two-legged creature...

Fate brings us together more often than I'd like.

Fate prevails over everyone, even gods and demiurges. The All-Mother is also subject to its unstoppable power. Who knows what's in store?

If you were destined to go to Eden, it was inevitable.

If we had the weaver's looms since the time of Old Isa, we would know what threatens us. But a lot of knowledge is lost, and it's hard to imagine the future.

You and I saw the future where Nihaz took over. Horizon or New Isa - it didn't matter. The darkness won. I know what Alice told you - the guest from the future whose Thread was broken. This is another version.

Your destiny is to be a Weaver, therefore your choice will be decisive.
So, what do you have to say?

Ugh, I don't even know what to tell you...

Alright, let's stay calm...

NO! WHAT IN THE WORLD ARE YOU DOING?!

YOU HAD A SIMPLE TASK - TO FIND MY MOTHER AND SECURE HELP!!

WHAT IS CATHERINA DOING?

Go back to Eden immediately and order them to stop stealing the Ambrosia... from these... natives.

Yes, I understand that my mother can be difficult, but all you need to do is arrange for her to come here. I'll figure the rest out myself.

Catherina went off her rocker, apparently. Power drove her crazy. But that can be fixed - we already gave her a thrashing once.

What else do we have?

An ambitious imperial general? A greedy Free Trader?

Small fry.

I think you can easily deal with this whole rabble. So your task is to help the All-Mother get rid of especially impudent invaders, and then ask her to come to Sarnaut.

That's some bullshit, to be honest. Talking trees, gods, planets... If I didn't know you, I'd think that someone with a massive hangover was telling me their dream.

And Skulnar stayed there, you say?

Well, I wouldn't advise you to believe the Xadaganians. This Felix is a piece of work, I've heard all about him. In fact, he is aiming for Yasker's position, and this... Ex-pe-di-tion... is a good way to win authority. And together with Catherina, they might even try and crush the League.

If what you say about talking logs is true, then they are pretty good guys. Not as good as the Orcs, of course, but still decent warriors!

I take it Skulnar is on their side? Then we need to help them! And punching Xadaganians is a good cause all around.

The old goat is still alive? Can he even raise the belt?

It's the same thing every time. He should retire already. It's rightly said that if an orc lived to twenty five, he's not an orc but a piece of shit! And he's almost forty. Senility is around the corner!

Guess I'm going to punch him in the face the next time I see him. I owe him a few grudges.

The old man? Oh, I'll do it myself. I've been thinking of visiting my ancestral home, so to speak. It's the same thing every time. He should retire already. It's rightly said that if an orc lived to twenty five, he's not an orc but a piece of shit! And he's almost forty. Senility is around the corner!

Tell him I haven’t punched him in a while, and I'm itching to kick his ass. Gotta be a sign that I'll see him soon.

Catherina should be fully supported in her activities. The Ambrosia has already proved its effectiveness in the field of mana engineering, and we need a constant influx of it, which means Eden is a key point for our interests.

I think Felix is a fairly experienced warrior who knows what he's doing, but their forces might be unequal. We have a small expeditionary force on our side, and theirs are the resources of their world and the goddess who created it.

 I believe you can handle this mission and provide our world with the Ambrosia.
This flower of the Great Tree contains All-Mother's memories.

But you are not ready to see them yet.

Hinanna strove to be equal to her elder sister. She strove to outperform her. At that time Hirkalla already possessed the power of Darkness and ruled the Death world. Jealous of her sister's might, Hinanna wanted to seize what she posessed.

She gathered secret forces, wore her best clothes and jewelry, and embarked on the journey. She approached the colossal gates of the underground world, awoke the guardian by a loud banging, and fiercely demanded that he let her in.

One cannot enter the Death world and disobey the laws. Hinanna had to give all her clothes and jewels along with all her powers to pass the gates of Ganzir. And she fell under the power of the Death world, ruled by her sister. The young goddess never expected this. She became dead while being alive, and condemned herself to a worse fate.

I knew not what became of Sarn. I knew not of the fate of the younger daughter. Although I felt sorry for the gullible Hinanna that fell victim to her own stupidity, there was a much worse threat hanging over our worlds. The Architect came from far-away world. The heartless Order, where mind and will were one. Nihaz and I had to fight the invader.

I came out of my shelter every once in a while. Having destroyed an emissary of the new enemy, I felt that my lost daughter and a forgotten friend were once again close. When the ship of the missionary of the Order was torn to pieces by my Great Trees, he fell like a ball of fire upon the lifeless world. I gazed upon the empty ground and saw only vile dragons, loyal to Nihaz. I realized that they would summon their King, and left this world. I returned to Eden but never gave up my attempts at finding my lost daughter.

What is mortal's eternity to me? Only an instant. It's been five thousand years. My heart is still yearning.

All that has been created will perish.

All that has perished will be recreated.

The existence is a great circle. There is no creation without destruction. There is no destruction without creation.

The circle has no beginning or end.

The divine couple has always existed. All-Mother and Father Time. I, All-Mother, is the goddess of life and creation. Father Time is the god of death and destruction. Together we led our worlds through the cycles of births and deaths. We created and destroyed.

We were not alone. Our passion gave birth to our divine children, subject to us. Each of them played their own role. Each of them obeyed the common laws. There were twelve Domains in my hierarchy. Each Domain was responsible for a single power. Each Domain had a master.

Only I, All-Mother, the goddess of creation, and my divine husband, Father Time, the god of destruction, were eternal Lords of our Domains. Other gods were immortal and lived very long lives, which ultimately had to be over. The circle has always spun, and gods were destined to die.

Many years have passed.

Each world was once created. At the moment of creation its death was predefined. Father Time knows no pity. He watches the sand of time in his hourglass.

There's a point in the circle that is called Judgment Time. Ancient prophecies come true. The war is raging in multiple worlds. The Twilight of the Gods is impending. This is the time when the figures on the board change. The wheel turns. Those who was on top will fall. Those who were beneath will rise.

This is the fate of the world, predetermined by me, All-Mother, and by Father Time. Evil against Good. Evil rises over Good for just an instant but its fate is predetermined as well. It will fall. The Good will win, there is no other way. The sacrifice is great but day comes after night. This is the law that we established.

This is what happened last time. The ancient God of Darkness, now known as the Forgotten, has risen in all of his power. The worlds, possessed by legions of the Darkness, are burning. But the God of Light Sarn has also risen. He headed the resistance against the Darkness and destroyed the Forgotten once and for all. This was predetermined. Everything that's happened is just as we planned.

The new day has come. The circle is spinning once again.

Many gods fell in the war with the Forgotten. Many worlds were destroyed. The survivors gathered in Eidos, where the primal images of creation are stored. Everything that had to be created originally existed in Eidos.

I set to work, willing to create new worlds instead of what was destroyed. I created the twelve inner worlds first, in accordance with the number of Domains. Each of them should have been led by one of the survivors or newly born gods.

Sarn was one of the survivors, the greatest hero of the past war. He rightfully took the place of the God of Light.

Father Time and I chose two young goddesses among the new gods: Hirkalla and Hinanna. They were supposed to lead the Domains of Life and Death.

Only the Domain of the Forgotten, the Domain of Darkness remained unowned. None of the surviving gods wanted to take his place.

Millions of years passed since the victory over Forgotten. The new god of the Domain of Darkness appeared. Hinanna, the younger sister, brought him to the door of Eidos. We accepted him and allowed him to take the vacant place. Each of the gods was supposed to played a role. The God of Darkness was accepted in our domain.

Hinanna's decision did not surprise me. She was a beautiful young goddess, stubborn, moody, gullible, and impulsive. She traveled across the worlds a lot, found her chosen ones among gods and mortals, toyed with their lives.

At some point, the mysterious God of Darkness attracted her attention. No one knew where he had come from. Some thought that he was mortal, who managed to become a god. This was extremely rare back then.

Hinanna showed him the way to Eidos, even though her sister Hirkalla pointed out that his intentions weren't pure. She thought that he was weird and scary so she decided to keep an eye on him.

Hinanna was happy to see new faces. She and Nihaz, the God of Darkness, traveled between worlds, watched the fates of mortals, learned their secrets, discovered ancient artifacts of eons.

The power of the new God of Darkness grew by the year. Ancient monsters, who still remembered the Forgotten, accepted him. None of us had any objections. The Darkness was the natural opposite of the Light, and the Domain required a master. At that time Father Time and I considered him an ordinary "Master of Darkness," one of many. As other gods, he was supposed to start a war and fight the Light, and finally perish, like the Forgotten before him. This is what we thought, and never worried.

Only Hirkalla sensed that the circle has changed its spin. We considered her too young to rule the Domain of Death. She oversaw the Guardians of Ganzir, who ruled the post-mortal fates of all living in our worlds. Thanks to this, she saw that Nihaz was helping, teaching, and protecting mortals as best he could in his travels with Hinanna. She realized that their faith in him gave him even more power.

In doubt, Hirkalla decided to have a straight talk. She gathered herself, and went to the throne of Darkness to dispel her fears. At that time, Hinanna took interest in another mortal, and the God of Darkness was left alone.

They had a long conversations. Hirkalla gave him her doubts, and Nihaz answered them. Few people knew what they were talking about but Hinanna returned from her journey and witnessed the end of the talk.

The younger sister learned that Nihaz wanted to overthrow me, All-Mother, and Father Time. He didn't think much of our concept of the world. He mocked the idea of the circle and the renewal of worlds. Nihaz believed that the gods should make mortals our equals, teach them the laws of creation and eternal life.

Hinanna rushed to our divine throne straight away to warn us of the betrayal. I got furious and ordered to bring Hirkalla before my eyes.

She was brought to the trial, and accused of being insubordinate. She silently took her sentence and was off to the exile. Since that day, Nihaz was persona non grata in Eidos. Unfortunately, by that time many of the gods were on his side. The creators that didn't want the destruction of their worlds listened to him. This rebel was loved not only by those who belonged to the Darkness but also Chaos and Death. Even gods of elements joined his riot.

I didn't expect him to turn to mortals, helping them fight monsters and improving their lives. His name was praised for giving knowledge and teaching crafts. Nihaz's gifts were poisonous but he gave them generously to his followers. Mortals, who sought immortality and divinity, raised a riot.

Anxiously we have watched from our thrones the growing numbers of Nihaz's army. There was still time until another cycle of destruction and rebirth, but this war couldn't wait. It came to us.

Hirkalla, our beloved daughter, then joined Nihaz. With all her heart, she accepted his teaching about the freedom of choice, the breaking of the great circle, and giving the mortals freedom to become gods.

Our worlds were thrown in a long war. Nihaz and the other gods fought against me and Father Time. Sarn, the God of Light, was one of his main enemies at this war.

Nihaz's efforts have given fruit. Gods died one after another. The most terrible thing happened when Nihaz and the others dealt the fatal blow to Father Time. They got him near the World of Destruction, where he engaged in a battle with the Darkness. Only God can kill a God. Nihaz inflicted a fatal blow to Father Time, already wounded, and took away his power. Since then, he became more than the God of Darkness, but hasn't reached what he was looking for.

We were wondering what he really wanted. Sarn suggested that his true goal was to raise his own power. He destroyed many gods, including his former allies, Gods of Death and Chaos, and took their power.

Worried by what happened to my husband, I avoided any battles. Eden, the world of Life, became my shelter. The story was simple. I knew that my daughter Hinanna would gain enough experience and wisdom, so eventually she was to become the owner of the divine garden. The Garden of Eden was hidden from Nihaz. Everyone was safe. The war was continued by Sarn, Nihaz's complete opposite. He successfully destroyed legions of darkness, marching through our worlds.

But even a great warrior can fall prey to betrayal. There was a traitor in our ranks. To my surprise, it was Hinanna. Jealous of her sister and her glory with Nihaz, she decided to switch to the stronger side. Hinanna lured Sarn into a trap. After fighting Nihaz, the God of Light was captured.
No one dares to give me orders!
No, wait, wait! Don't leave me here...

No... The Darkness took him... I stayed here...

She beckons with promises, but I no longer believe in such things.

It doesn't matter, I was once the ruler of a kingdom far away from here...

After death, I... got lost... But death is only the beginning of the journey. In the end, I was carried away to the Star Trail...

Where I met it. Darkness.

It's very interested in people like me... It wants to raise an army. Go to war against the gods of Light and Order. Sweep them off their thrones.

I don't want to be part of someone else's plans...

Moreover, it's more interested in... you.

We all thought so at the beginning of our journey. The light gave me strength, but my path... led me into darkness.

The same fate awaits you!
Keep looking! They are around here somewhere!
I did not believe tales of treasures and miracles. I thought they were in great trouble, so I hurried to help. I did not stop to think how I would return home...
Where are my knights? Where are my warriors?! There were thirty three of them...
I didn't want this, Father! Will you ever forgive me? Damn Wanderer! He fooled us all!
Damned yokels! What do you even know?! I would have accomplished so much more, were it not for the cursed patriarchy!!
Oh, it’s you again! Well? Have you found the treasure? Yes... Go three steps to the south, five to the east... A treasure! A treasure full of June coins! No one will leave here alive, you hear me?!
Great, now we can rest easy!
Great, now we can rest easy!
And again the trenches of Metalville, the whistle of shrapnel, and the rumble of artillery... Stand fast! We will not retreat from these ruins. The attack of the Reds will be repulsed!
Yes, yes, children... True wisdom is ever to be found in simplicity.
I am Lord Kargalas, and no one dares to set foot on my lands without my permission! My castle always towered over the fertile valley where the peasants grew their crops...
Do you hear the music? Ah, this melody, it is so sweet... Come, come, traveler. Sit down with us at the banquet table, but do not ask about the dishes that are served to you...
Ugh... It's so cold... What have we done? We shouldn't have opened the gates to the world of ice and death...
True evil lurks in the ancient ruins! Beware!   Beware of abandoned palaces, beware of crossroads...
Maximum energy! Stop the machine! Navigator! The equipment! Two hundred. Two hundred what? What about the equipment?
Hey, you want me to answer your question? The truth is simple - and the cards will show it? Do you wish to know the future? Foresee what's coming?

Buy cheap, sell high... I traveled many roads along Umoir. Few people glorify a greedy merchant - skalds will not mention him in a song, the chronicler will not write about him... But aren't we the salt of the earth?
What is this evil sorcery? Begone! What's going on here? Strange things are afoot in the Kanian state...

Yasker is too weak to fight the Goddess of Darkness. But Catherina and I are going to challenge her!

As for the war here in Eden... It doesn't change anything!

On the contrary, our task has become even more important. To gather strength to fight this… Hirkalla, we need even more Ambrosia! And even if I stay here alone, I will continue to harvest it!

I hope you're still on our side.

Unthinkable! Without the All-Mother our worlds will be swallowed by darkness! We need to find a way to tell the other gods what happened...

As for the war with the Expedition... What happened doesn't change anything!

On the contrary, our task has become even more important. To gather strength to fight this… Hirkalla, we need to protect Eden! And even if I stay here alone, I will continue to defend it!

I hope you're still on our side.

quests: Battle for Ambrosia: Capturing the Sources

t:
Hi!

I'm one of Sarn's followers. We're here to resurrect our god. But we need more ambrosia.

I have ancient sacred garments, and also outfits of pathetic heretics, the trophies from the captured ships.

I can trade with you if you can get local currencies, Dendrite Coins or Tears of All-Mother. I could trade them for ambrosia. Otherwise, I'm sorry, that wouldn't be possible.

Hello! I'm Zlata Zharova, head of supply division.

I'm responsible for uniform and other useful stuff for the Expedition.

I could sell some of it to you if you have Dendrite Coins, the local currency. By Catherina's order, this is the currency we're using here to avoid mix-up with lots of other Sarnaut currencies.

Elemental worlds suffered the most. They were sources of divine energy needed to create other worlds, so every party was hunting for them. Eira loved freedom too much to obey anyone.

However, Eira, the powerful leader, was one of the perished gods. Nihaz took part of her power that he later accumulated in the materialized Seal.

Eira was a furious goddess, the ruler of winds and hurricanes. She didn't care much of mortals' needs and lives. She found her tragic end in one of the battles. Ermay, cunning and slick, replaced her. Her former subordinate, he knew what his followers needed. Their number began to grow. He is the patron of merchants, crooks, and philosophers. Ermay is considered to lead Sparks along star tracks.

Anrok is one of the worlds where the Light fights against the Darkness. It has a rich history. Initially inhabited by refugees of other worlds, eventually it began its own way of development. Powerful mages and brave warriors fought one another to rule the world. Many were tempted by the Darkness, others rejected temptations. Do I need to tell you all stories of the world?

About brothers who fought to death for the throne? About the daughter who took back her father's kingdom by force? There are so many stories...

Ardan is the world where gods participate in everything. The laws of All-Mother are same in all worlds. Some smaller domains are often divided by forces, same as the inner worlds. These smaller forces make weird alliances, which might differ from those here. But the darkness is always darkness. Thankfully, Nihaz isn't omnipresent or omniscient. His dark minions act by the laws we know, even though their lord wants to break the Great Circle.

Ardan is the world where his effort doesn't bear fruit. It still lives the rightful life.

The darkness is eternal but mortals can fight it.

Ascolet is another world where the confrontation of two forces predetermine the existence. At fate would have it, these forces are exact opposite. Just think. There are two alliances. One belongs to the mages that resemble your Great Mages. The other belongs to proud kings, who put the ban on any witchery whatsoever. It is also made impossible by a mysterious artifact at the border between the enemies.

Moreover, each alliance is supported by mysterious forces of Order and Chaos, and their feud has lasted much longer than the feud between knights and sorcerers.

Atla is faithful to All-Mother, although the mortals there have no idea of her existence. Each of the outer worlds is unique, and they all have something in common. Such races as elves or humans aren't uncommon in other worlds. Creators tend to repeat and reproduce their best creations. The prototypes of all living things were stored in Eidos.

I think even in your world, the races have fought wars to rule your world. This is what happened in Atla. The elves were banished from their lands by a young race of people. They tried to reclaim what was lost. This led to the conflict that involved all people of Atla. This war was a battleground for the living as well as for the divine powers. The Light fought against the Darkness. The Chaos tried to destroy the Order.

This world of red ocean and white sand, dotted with pillars of stone, is under attack by monsters from worlds ruled by chaos. However, there is hope - the inhabitants of the world have found a way to fight back. I heard you use ingenious technical devices in Sarnaut - they are like a second set of clothes for you. The inhabitants of Ayanami have gone much further - their suits are huge structures created to fight against the giants of the world of Chaos. It's surprisingly effective, though I don't think mortals' addiction to these tricks will do them any good.

But now the hope of that world rests only on those who know how to manage such mechanisms. It is a pity that this world does not have its own protector gods, and they can only hope that the devices they have created will be stronger than monsters.

Sherk is the world of Chaos. A planet of diversity, with swamps, lava fields, and glaciers.

All kinds of monsters are always born here. Nihaz was the first to notice it. He wanted an army that would allow him to fight with Sarn and Juvius as equals.

He reached agreement with the numerous monsters surprisingly fast. It wasn't enough to bring them to his army. He needed something to teach them to act together. And that's where the Dark God failed. Chaos can't be harnessed. The eternal riot is the essence of it. Armies of Chaos fought with each other more often than with the army of All-Mother that were united and loyal to their leaders.

Of course, the creatures of Chaos were strong and capable of doing a lot of harm. The worst of them was the leader of the Chaos Domain, Sherk. He was a giant, sleeping on the ocean floor. Nihaz awakened him and sent him to assault one of the strongholds of the Order. It was a miracle when Juvius's armies repelled the powerful god, who inflicted madness only by his appearance on the battlefield.

Sherk gave in, and Nihaz dealt the fatal blow that took some of his power.

Sherk died, but his place was taken by someone else. Amaya, the treacherous goddess of Chaos, the ancestor of a fireskinned race, took advantage of the situation and gained control over Chaos. She had never trusted Nihaz. She realized that his goals were larger than anything that Chaos creations might ever want. Now that she began to act on her own, Nihaz became her enemy. That was the point when the Chaos began to fight for itself in this war.

Fiore is the source of life among the worlds. The world of creation was too valuable to be affected by war. Nihaz put a real effort to understand its mysteries but failed.

Abandoned by its goddess, Fiore gives birth to numerous new life forms, transferred then to new worlds.

It's amazingly peaceful, although its visitors told about unimaginable images that came to them. These are the Spinning Wheel, and the Wheel, and the Source of Sparks, and other mysteries.

Darien was one of the outer worlds, where Nihaz's promises gave bitter fruit. Like many others, this world was divided by hostile elements.
 The rivalry between the four siblings, each representing their own element, resulted in the emergence of the fifth element. It became the base for the new order, the heartless technology, hostile towards everyone and everything.
 Later this war extended to nearby worlds and became the arena of a great rivalry, which was no longer about victory. Both parties wanted complete destruction of one another.

Ossu is the world of Darkness. One might think that it's the center of Nihaz's power, the destruction of which would lead Enod and Inis to victory in the Great War.

But it would be tragically, dramatically wrong. Ossu is the dead world, empty, save for shadows. Everyone who gets here eventually gets sick. If I understand the Sage correctly, the disease is the same as Tep's plague. The only difference is that the dead Sparks don't gather in Pyramids. They get affected by the Darkness and become base for dark soul creations.

Nihaz has taken everything he ever wanted from Ossu. He doesn't want complete power over the Darkness, unlike the Forgotten. He wants something else.

Eresh. The sinister world of Death. It hasn't always been like this. A long while ago it was the dreamy world that gave rest to those who were ready to be reborn in their own body. It gave the eternal peace to those, whose time has come to an end. It was possible thanks to the guardians of Ganzir and soul drivers. Everything changed when Eresh, the leader of guardians, gave in to Nihaz's pleads and faced All-Mother and Father Time. Hardly anyone was aware of the Dark God's cunning. He clashed Death Guards and Dragons of the Void. Then his promised daughter Hirkalla took Eresh's main weapon and symbol of power over his world, the Scythe of Death. Hirkalla slain the High Guardian of Death and took the throne that was promised to her. She ruled the bigger part of Eresh from the Palace of Ganzir. Only Shetius, a senior guard, refused to swear allegiance. He had way fewer followers.

Eresh has changed. Nihaz and Hirkalla abandoned their duty and used the Sparks, imprisoned there, for their dark purposes.

As a consequence, Eresh was no longer the final destination for the dead Sparks. Now they were scattered throughout the universe, each attracted to the most powerful center of attraction.

Dizz is the world of Destruction. Father Time's throne. Father Time's grave. The divine spouse of All-Mother fell from the hand of treacherous Nihaz, who took part of his power. Only god can kill a god. No one suspected that Time itself could be killed as well. Father was the end and beginning of the Great Circle. He kept the time bent into a circle. Every ending was also a beginning of something and each beginning ultimately led to an end. Now it's all different. The time broke the circle and went on into the Eternity. This is the straight line without an end.

Nihaz's victory meant something else. The dragons of the Void have witnessed the defeat of their Lord and sided with the God of Darkness.

These timeless mighty creatures were the essence of Destruction. They inhabited Dizz and nearby worlds, including the world of dragons, known as Servants of Nihaz. After the death of Time, they all were on his side.

It is usually the responsibility of the gods to protect their worlds, but in this world, things turned out differently - a treaty was made that placed this duty on the shoulders of mortals. A limited confrontation is preferable to a large-scale war with unknown consequences - both the defenders and the conquerors decided so.

The result was a tournament. The world whose representatives win this tournament is declared the winner and can decide the fate of the defeated. I believe it to be reasonable, because that's how the fate of the worlds is decided by heroes and the gods these heroes serve. Everything is in accord with the precepts of the All-Mother.

Unfortunately, not everything is as good on Ditsu Vango. Having failed to defeat the defenders of this world in a fair fight, the conquerors resorted to numerous tricks, trying to circumvent the rules of the tournament. So far, their intrigues have ended in failure, but who knows what will happen in the future?

This world is full of magic. Despite that, the inhabitants of Dunkel have very advanced technology. Perhaps it's because magic is perceived by them as something unnatural, otherworldly. This world is indeed a little darker than usual. In addition to humans, it is inhabited by a large number of small races that live their own lives and do not claim supremacy. They hide behind the walls of houses where humans live, inhabit dense forests where humans do not set foot.

But sometimes their paths cross. "Miracles" take place then. Humans are always amazed whenever they meet a part of their world they normally ignore. In addition to the minor races, Dunkel is full of undead that are more friendly than hostile, and also talking animals - individuals that are sentient for some strange reason.

Erde. An elemental world, a source of building materials for other worlds. The famous Horn of Abundance comes from here. It's always full of the great gifts of the Earth. It was once ruled by the horned god Erd, the keeper of the treasures, who watched his lands and couldn't tolerate intruders. The Great War knows no pity. The harsh xenophobic god perished in a battle with the Darkness.

He was replaced by Theona, a young goddess of Gardens and Groves, a younger sister of Hirkalla and Hinanna. She wanted to make the suffering world beautiful again. She covered it with fruit trees, abundant meadows, and green fields. Unlike Eden, full of pristine forests, Erde is a farmland, cultivated by hardworking people. However, there are people, marked by Nihaz. They want to explode the ground and mind minerals and gems, like in the old days. Erde is a safe world but not ideally safe.

Eshan. I have a lot to say about it. The struggle of the opposing forces, the Order and Chaos, the Light and Darkness, is taking place there. History of this world has been dark. Nihaz couldn't lead its people astray like in Anrok. It was affected by the Chaos much more than by the Darkness.

I heard that Sarn was imprisoned in the heart of your world. The same way as the powerful god of Chaos was imprisoned here. He did everything in his power to break free. Just like Sarn.

Unfortunately for this world's people, there was a breach in his prison. Creation of Chaos used it to enter the mortal worlds.

They reached the highest success after one of the queens got under the influence of a mighty general of the Chaos armies and helped them carry out their plans.

Another world that doesn't have a lot of magic. It's frozen on the edge between what you call "technological progress" and the old ways conforming to the All-Mother's precepts. Yes, Fabella is one step away from taking the path that Nihaz led his worlds to, and so far no one can say in which direction the unstable balance will shift.

The difference between Fabella and many worlds is that the race inhabiting it is divided into many peoples, and each of them has created their own civilization. Now in this world, wars for supremacy are raging. Swords cross, bows sing, all to determine who will prevail.

Each of these peoples considers themselves the most worthy. They all have their own advantages and disadvantages. Who will win? Who will lose? It's not clear yet.

Pyro is the unfriendliest of the elemental worlds.

The god Pyro once was the guardian of the Forge of the Gods, where they created artifacts used to make other worlds. The enraged fire giant guarded his lands of deserts and lava lakes. Pyro was one of Nihaz's primary targets shortly after the Great War began. The Darkness came to Pyro and destroyed ancient cities, ravaged these lands, erased the only remaining life from it.

Nihaz destroyed Pyro and gained power of Fire. Time passed, and the Darkness was gone. Pyro began to come back to life. Survivors gathered in underground towns or high towers where the surface heat was not so burning.

The new goddess, Afeta, took place of the fallen deity. She knew the metalworking. She created masterpieces. I personally can't appreciate what's made of dead metal, but still.

Regardless of her skills, she failed to set life on good course in Pyro. The underground city and tower rulers took power in their hands. Their hearts were possessed by Nihaz's darkness. Their wars with each other and other elemental worlds led to numerous calamities.

What kind of world is this? The border of savagery and civilization where dust, gold, and weapons form the basis of life. Harsh conditions breed harsh morals, and here being true to one's word isn't worth much, so in fights beloved by the inhabitants of this world, the winner is usually the one that plays dirty. However, there is beauty here, too - spaces untouched by humans, wild animals that are not pushed out by the cars you love so much. It is a pity that none of this is valued as much as gold. This is truly cursed metal, but for some reason it's loved the most by the inhabitants of this world.

Another world of technology. However, on Girheim, it took on a very bizarre look. Due to the fact that this world is poor in natural resources, its inhabitants are forced to make do with what they have. Yes, they build their machines, but those machines are based on different principles compared to whatever is used in other technological worlds.

Perhaps this is precisely the reason the technology of this world is more like magic than the technology in other worlds. Based on what I've seen, I can say that it's similar to your manatech, only instead of magic it works on the power of heated water.

Indeed, in any world, mortals will find any way to achieve what they want!

The inhabitants of this world also build airships, only they rise into the air with the help of special balls filled with gases that are lighter than air.

Cyros is one of the outer worlds, possessed by Darkness. This world remembers and respects the will of All-Mother. Its dwellers are attacked by sinister creatures beneath the surface. It's riddled with tunnels and caves, opening on the surface. Defenders of this world are fighting against the dungeon kings... not very successfully.

A new war began when one of these Guardians began an aggressive campaign against the human Empire protected by the power of one of the light goddesses. He managed to achieve a lot and defeated the other dungeon masters, but in the end, he himself became a victim of betrayal.

I know that your world was broken up by the Great Mages, craving for power. They dealt irreparable damage in their pursuit of power. Sarnaut is not the only world where this has happened. Carpey was also destroyed after the mages instigated a war over leadership.
 Each of them wanted to take the world's power, but in the end, one of them cast a destructive spell that was supposed to stop the others. Instead, the spell broke the world. Its shards were filled with monsters that attacked the greedy mages.

Are there any worlds completely possessed by the Darkness? Yes, there are. Crippla is one of them. This world is old enough, and it's gone way beyond All-Mother's plan. It's not the only problem. Evil is done openly in Crippla. Dark cults worshipping the dark gods seized power, and the ancient monsters awakened. One by one, the cities fell under their control. Bloody sacrifices began.

The God of Death has supreme power here, which might have been the reason for all of the above. He forgot his duty, and he simply loves torturing mortals. His power over the souls of the dead allows him to raise the undead who hate the guts of the living.

Those who saw the doomed world understand what we are dealing with.

The last data I received mentions a certain avenger. He was one of the members of the cult organized by this sinister god but, like his friends, he was betrayed and killed. He rose from the dead, thirsting for revenge, and succeeded - the deity of death, which neglected his duties, was destroyed.

Lafia might seem a happy little world.

It might be true. At first sight. Its people don't suffer from wars or disasters. This is a happy place, although there are the poor and unhappy here, as well.

There's another problem. The souls of people here have long been consumed by Nihaz's darkness. All they want is pleasure and joy. Their world is full of fun devices designed for pleasure.

The price for it is emptiness inside. They don't want anything in life but to gain more, take more, consume more.

Your world could have gone the same way. Several safe centuries, and you all end up like Lafia!

For some reason, the messenger sent to this world became extremely interested in one of the completely unremarkable mortals who was considered a failure even among their fellow tribesmen. The Herald discovered that it was this mortal's Thread of Destiny that was intimately intertwined with the fate of the world. The tapestry woven by fate is bizarre, if it is true.

I hear there are vampires in Sarnaut. They aren't unique to your world. They sucked out dry almost all people of Lacona.

I suppose, the root cause of vampirism lies in Ossu. Another All-Mother's world is a haven for many dark creatures of the ancient eons. Vampires are perfect spreaders of the Darkness. They can hide out for a long time, and then come out and infect everyone around them.

That's what happened in Lacona. According to my sources, one of the most powerful vampires awoke there. Whether he belonged to another world or was born on Lacona, I do not know.

But he infected most of the people before they hunted him down.

Alas, some of the vampires escaped. Several centuries later, a much more powerful burst of vampirism broke out on Lacona and swallowed the entire world.

You are now in Eden. It's All-Mother's divine garden she created for her beloved daughter. And the ideal hideout from the Darkness. Eden is a secret world. Nihaz has no idea where it is. The void between the worlds is endless. The number of worlds evolving around their Suns is endless. Even if Nihaz has all the time in the world, he won't be able to find All-Mother.

Nihaz's followers have been looking for All-Mother for millions of years. Every time she managed to escape.

Eden has a perfect symbiosis of plants and animals. They all exist together, and they can't do without one another. Eden's greatest mystery is the Great Tree. The embodiment of All-Mother's divine powers. The amazing plants give birth to the forces of Creation and Life.

The smallest Tree sprout can take root in the void and create matter around it.

All-Mother's great plan is to plant the Tree sprouts in all worlds, thus bringing the life in all corners of the Universe.

Enod is the world of Light. Sarn's creation. His very triumph. There's no place for shadows in Enod. Its multiple Suns shine the light on the snow-white sky, and the golden cities of wise alvies lie beneath them.

But this world isn't as serene as ours. Enod existed long before Nihaz began his rebellion. The dark servants knew very well where it was. It's a challenge for every follower of the God of Darkness, and their effort to destroy this world is untold.

The worst part is that Sarn is gone. Enod has no patron anymore. Only four tetranonymous, his loyal followers, could gather an army large enough to defend the world. It was like that until the new God of Light, the glorious Eton, came to replace Sarn.

Now Eton and his loyal tetranonymous continue to fight Nihaz. They fought back his attacks, led by the evil Hirkalla, and began an onslaught, attacking their armies in many worlds.

Marn is an outer world, where two forces are fighting. It's hard to name these forces, though. It's a complex mixture of Darkness, Chaos, and elemental magic. I hear, there was once a Leper in Sarnaut that corrupted the living, turning them into monsters.

We have something similar here. It's called Blight. The curious effect is that any magic triggers the Blight to spread. As a consequence, all magic is banned by the authorities of the world. There's an Order that hunts down all kinds of sorcerers and mages.

They prefer to solve their issues with steel weapons. Even a trace of the Blight can't make it inside this world.

Your Spark might have something in common with this world and the element of Air.

Among the dragons that arrived with Nihaz to Sarnaut, Alsirr would be the closest to you.

Your Spark might have something in common with this world and the element of Chaos.

Among the dragons that arrived with Nihaz to Sarnaut, Sargas would be the closest to you.

Your Spark might have something in common with this world and the element of Creation.

Among the dragons that arrived with Nihaz to Sarnaut, Situla would be the closest to you.

Your Spark might have something in common with this world and the element of Darkness. Beware!

Among the dragons that arrived with Nihaz to Sarnaut, Zuben would be the closest to you.

Your Spark might have something in common with this world and the element of Death.

Among the dragons that arrived with Nihaz to Sarnaut, Nashira would be the closest to you.

Your Spark might have something in common with this world and the element of Destruction.

Among the dragons that arrived with Nihaz to Sarnaut, Rukbat would be the closest to you.

Your Spark might have something in common with this world and the element of Earth.

Among the dragons that arrived with Nihaz to Sarnaut, Elnat would be the closest to you.

Your Spark might have something in common with this world and the element of Fire.

Among the dragons that arrived with Nihaz to Sarnaut, Sheratan would be the closest to you.

Your Spark might have something in common with this world and the element of Life. You're just like us!

Among the dragons that arrived with Nihaz to Sarnaut, Revati would be the closest to you.

Your Spark might have something in common with this world and the element of Light.

Among the dragons that arrived with Nihaz to Sarnaut, Regul would be the closest to you.

Your Spark might have something in common with this world and the element of Order.

Among the dragons that arrived with Nihaz to Sarnaut, Sirma would be the closest to you.

Your Spark might have something in common with this world and the element of Water.

Among the dragons that arrived with Nihaz to Sarnaut, Tegmin would be the closest to you.

Almid is one of the most technologically advanced worlds. I'm not surprised. There's no magic that could make its dwellers' lives easier. There's no magic in this world whatsoever!

Many people and many countries are allied there. They always create new weapons and armored machinery, deadlier and complex.

Fortunately, they haven't yet destroyed their own world, but it isn't due to them being particularly reasonable. Outsiders interfered at some point.

A while ago they stole a crystal of ambrosia left at the battlefield where All-Mother and Nihaz's army fought. Outsiders cracked some of its properties and managed to grow more crystals, even though this form of divine life energy is only a reflection of its true self. So they spread ambrosia across other worlds, because all worlds can give their own Life power.

One of the crystals ended up on Almid. Due to the magic power, it began to grow. Just like you, people discovered its properties and started a hunt. It was the reason for more conflicts. The war has been on for a whole century!

Don't expect any hospitality from Inis if you ever make it there. Its dwellers are harsh and quick to judge. Their trial is just but not exactly merciful.

There's a reason for the harshness. None of the inner worlds suffered as much as Inis. This stronghold of Order lost its god Juvius, who fell victim to Nihaz.

After Juvius perished, Inis suffered a lot of invasions. At first, Hirkalla's Dark army set foot in these lands. Then Amaya brought her creatures of Chaos to these lands. And finally, Inis was ravaged by legions of architects, enforcing their own vision of Order.

The influence of an egregore as powerful as the Architect sapped the strength of Inis. However, the world hasn't lost heart. Young Nemia, the new goddess, took over the domain of Order.

She turned to the outer worlds. Her ambassadors started recruiting an army for the upcoming war. Thanks to her iron willpower, the world got their own legion that counterattacked the enemy. Eton, the got of Light, allied with Nemia, and their armies fought together.

The Architect perished. He shattered into million shards, and the strength of the goddess of Order has grown exponentially. Now Nemia heads the army that successfully opposes Nihaz and his servants, destroying the blight of Chaos in the outer worlds. However, this war is far from being won.

Inis today is a military bastion, whose whole life yields to strict army regulations. The most popular punishment is death sentence. The life is regulated by a comprehensive Military Code.

Oztra. One of the worlds that has faced some tragic effects of advancement of science and technology. Even though Oztra was a world without magic, they created something truly devastating.

People, whose souls were affected by Nihaz's darkness, made a horrible discovery. In attempts to get a handle on stubborn neighbors, they found a way to split the smallest particle, the basis of everything in the Universe. This is how a weapon of unprecedented power was invented. As it turned out, splitting of the particle released a massive wave of energy.

They found a way to use it peacefully, of course... but its main application was to create weapons. Two empires, who, to be honest, didn't have so many issues, just kept arming themselves, striving to win the race. None of the sides survived to enjoy the victory.

The war started by mistake. The only consequence was destruction. The world of Oztra was incinerated by the advanced weapon. Its cities burned in blinding sheets of white flames. The survivors had to adjust to the new reality.

The luckiest ones managed to find refuge in bomb shelters. Others had to survive on the devastated surface. And then everything has fallen silent... until the new war, where people fought for the remaining resources.

Oztra will never change. Let its fate teach a good lesson to others.

Eidos is the primal world, which stores samples of everything that exists and ideas that could be incarnated in future worlds. This is the root cause why many things are very much alike in different worlds, even if their creators might add their personal touch.

Sadly, Nihaz chose Eidos as his primary target during the Great War. Thanks to the betrayal of one of All-Mother's daughters, he passed the ingenious defenses, put up by other gods, and sneaked into this world.

Eidos was conquered by the Darkness. Its secrets now belonged to the Dark God. It became the battlefield in the upcoming wars between Nihaz's followers and the worlds of Inis and Enod.

Finally, the battles of gods destroyed Eidos to the ground. Some of the things that had once belonged to Eidos were saved. They are now here, on Eden, waiting for All-Mother to begin a new cycle. Others were taken by Nihaz, giving him dangerous benefits in many regards.

Lucky for us, Nihaz cannot create Life. All he is capable of is corrupting and distorting other gods' creations. The knowledge of Eidos has made him a master of shifting and shaping the matter.

I have seen many alien worlds through the Tree, but few have surprised me. Ptolia is one of the worlds that managed to do that.

The amazing thirst for knowledge of the inhabitants of this world led to the fact that they began to collect it and store it. Perhaps the creator god of that world was the root cause, or maybe one of the mortals decided that this was worth doing, but in the end, this whole world became a giant library.

Here on Eden, we certainly think that our Trees are a much better way to gather information, but the Trees store images rather than words, so perhaps there is some sense in these actions. Perhaps, here is no such knowledge that would Ptolia does not possess - after all, the magically enchanted library is endless. Few people understand how new books appear there - perhaps the world itself absorbs the knowledge of our universe and turns it into written works...

I also know that Hirkalla and the Wanderer were in Ptolia and learned a lot there. This makes me think that perhaps such availability of knowledge is not always a good thing.

Nihaz covered your world under the twelve seals, and it was fascinating. While searching for similar cases in the Great Tree's memories, I came across a curious story. The world of Rhun was full of refugees from another world, driven away from their homeland by Nihaz's Darkness. After a while, they realized that his dark servants were following them. Fearing another invasion, they came up with the idea of their own Seals of Protection.

It is obvious that mortals aren't gods but their talents and skills were so good that they could seal twelve divine powers in twelve simple everyday objects.

And thus, the whole world was sealed. They isolated Rhun from the Darkness but as a consequence they were cut off the world magic. Alas! The objects, that were now seals, turned out to be quite fragile. Generations later, people forgot the very art of sealing the divine powers.

Mortals have short memories. Even though the creators made sure that the objects became hallowed relics, centuries later some of the Seals were broken in a fit of arrogance. It was much easier than in your world, but then again, the consequences weren't as grave. Little by little, the Darkness leaked into the world of Rhun. Its adherents insisted that the remaining Seals should be broken too. Sounds familiar, doesn't it?

I wish the memories weren't so sketchy. I have no idea how the story ended. Did the mortals defend their world? Did they fall in an uneven fight with the Darkness?

Any of the world histories is just a reflection of the Great War. Mortals may be unaware of Nihaz and Sarn, of All-Mother's great duty of looking after the Universal cycle of life... they may have their own beliefs, their own deities and demons. But then everything that has ever existed is just a part of the Great Circle. The powers of domains reflect in the fates of lesser deities.

Mortals often fall under the impression that Darkness, Chaos, and Death are evil in themselves. It's wrong. They're natural parts of the cycle. Darkness isn't evil per se. The evil was born when Nihaz decided to turn against All-Mother's will and transform everything that existed as he wanted.

Truth be told, when I hear about the deeds of lesser gods, I understand how mortals see evil in them.

The world of Sanctuar was the arena for massacre and bloodbath, for confrontation of all kids of gods. Most of them were the embodiment of evil and disgust, but their rivals, claiming to be warriors of Light and Warriors, were hardly any different.

Sarn in his eclipse of reason created monsters, similar to Chaos beasts from the outer worlds. They are known as demons to people of Sarnaut, whereas the true demons are the lesser gods of Sanctuar, deadly and savage, always at war. They are the ones responsible for a large part of Sanctuar's troubles.

A wise man told me about Tep, and his ideas and plans on Irdrich that he learned from someone. It's amazing, actually. The insane mage touched the mind of one of the Architect's shards, embraced his idea of the Absolute Order, and decided to carry it out on his own.

Something seems weird, tough. Tep has constructed an ideal virtual illusion for you, hasn't he? I wonder why he went with this particular paradise island with a struggle between Aviak tribes as a natural part of it. Has he considered it an ideal trap for all of you?

Perhaps, such interpretation of his ideas reveals the mystery of his sick mind. According to the Great Tree's memories, he isn't unique in this regard. The idea of settling everyone down in a virtual illusion of sorts isn't all that original. Some used magic for it, others developed sophisticated devices for that purpose.

This is what happened in the world of Synth, where a certain organization gained power. It connected all dwellers of this world to its own network of illusions via control implants in their heads. The much brighter and richer illusory world had nothing to with the dull and gray reality.

Similar to what happened on Irdrich, there were people that managed to escape from the virtual reality and start a resistance movement. Two powers clashed in a battle for minds and souls of this world's dwellers. I know not who won... but the very thought that it was once possible is scary.

Stargar is just one of the worlds we'll talk about if we remember it exists. The thing is, its inhabitants have long settled on many other worlds that surrounded Stargar, and now this world is only the center of their vast kingdom. Yes, the All-Mother seeks to prevent this, but to our surprise, the inhabitants of this world turned out to be very resistant to Nihaz's influence. And while their hope for the created mechanisms was great, they did not forget their roots.

However, in this story there was a moment when the darkness was stronger. Once upon a time, order in this star kingdom was provided by an order of knights, but there was a traitor in their ranks. He killed the king and almost ended the dynasty, and only a few of the knights were able to escape. The kingdom fell.

Since then, the influence of Darkness has only grown. The state that replaced the kingdom turned out to be unable to maintain the previous order, but in the darkest hour, a true heir was found and returned to power. Stargar became the way it was before. Who knows, maybe this world will be one of those that will help us defeat the Darkness?

When I first saw you in our world, found out your names and the differences between you, I couldn't help but remember this world.

It is pretty unique, though I've heard of others like it. Perhaps one of the gods who previously served Sarn is creating worlds based on a motif they discovered somewhere.

Yes, this note is also in Sarnaut, and it's embodied in the people of Kania. In Lightworld, people similar to your race found themselves at the center of events that determine the fate of the entire world. And it's just a forest country unknown to anyone and mostly forgotten. But it lies at the crossroads, and it's the reason the paths of some immortal heroes and the artifacts they kept converged there.

I often say that Chaos beings have infiltrated one of the worlds, and they are waging a war of conquest, but it's not only Chaos that brings destruction. Yes, Chaos is by nature more active, but Darkness also has its supporters.

More often than not, Nihaz's actions turn out to be a temptation, not a threat. While the God of Darkness prefers to act alone, and not through his minions, the Darkness has those who faithfully serve it. Many of those survived the fracture of the previous aeon when the Forgotten One was cast down.

Yes, the ancient god of Darkness left a mark, because the war he once started engulfed the entire universe. I don't know how the henchmen of Darkness made it into Tantibo, but I know there are many of them.

Lurking on the edge of reality, these creatures feed on the fears of mortals. Sparks are also nutritious for them, but they draw their strength from fear. Like the master of Darkness, they never act openly, because in the light they are weak, and in the shadows they are a deadly threat. And what's bad is that the inhabitants of this world are mostly unaware of them. Only a few lucky ones who survived the encounter with Darkness can tell the truth. But they are considered insane in this world.

Who is the true madman - the one who is aware of the danger or the one who doesn't see it, going straight into the trap?

It's strange seeing you among the dead. Among the metal bearers. I'm referring to the Arisen, of course. I took their destiny to the heart when I heard about it. They can't be blamed for taking their own fate. They died prematurely. Their immortality was, in fact, a curse rather than a blessing. Doomed for stagnation, they can't even reproduce. All of it is the consequence of Nihaz's influence, who corrupted Sarn's beautiful creation yet again.

I dug into the memory of the Great Tree and found another good example. Once upon a time there was a race in the world of Trogis. Just like the Arisen, they loved implanting new parts in their bodies.

What can be worse than a sinful synergy of flesh and metal?

When augmenting physical bodies with devices was normalized in the society, this race has become quite aggressive, turning Trogis into a militant world. Its dwellers mastered traveling to other worlds and started spreading their philosophy onto other societies.

Agwa is one of the friendliest inner worlds.

Once it was nothing but a vast ocean with occasional archipelagos raising from water here and there. The world's vigilant patron was the great god Agwas, who kept an eye out for any and all troubles. However, his first and foremost priority has always been the ocean and its depth. He didn't pay much attention to the mortals on the archipelagos.

Alas, even a bottomless ocean could not protect the world of Agwa against Hirkalla's army of Darkness. In pursuit of the aquatic elemental power, she emptied the ocean and challenged Agwas to a fight. And one of the keepers of inner worlds perished...

Hirkalla left. The storm has abated. The great god Neyes has become the new patron of the world. Neyes was spending more time with mortals than his predecessor, and the Agwa's mortals got to worship him more.

Neyes is a battle-hardened warrior. His exuberant nature matches the temper of the stormy ocean but he is merry and brave, and he loves boisterous worlds and competitions. The archipelagos are thriving under his rule. There's no more civil warfare. Everybody is busy doing their own thing. For fun, mostly.

The precepts of the All-Mother are unknown to this world. There has been a history of transgression of time parallels, wasteful use of elemental energy, and disruption of the balance of life and death, but only one has always lived up to its destiny: the never-ending battle between good and evil. The hero of the world Wuump is outwardly somewhat reminiscent of your Pridens - he always challenged evil in whatever form it manifested itself. I won't list all the dangers he faced. It also happened that one of the Ambrosia crystals, found in the underground network of caves, fell into the hands of an evil that dreamed of changing the world order.

But most of all I was surprised that this world had its own Great Tree, located in the center of the planet. As if an echo of Eden was in the mind of the one who created Wuump. Unfortunately, an evil spirit chose it as its fiefdom, inciting the creatures of this world to various lawless acts.

How this story ended is anyone's guess.

Did heavenly punishment fall on evil, or was the world swallowed up by a dark storm of Nihaz's minions?
